obligations.summary: Market surveillance authorities must carry out an evaluation of an AI system's compliance with all requirements and obligations under the Regulation when they have sufficient reason to consider it presents a risk, with particular attention to AI systems presenting a risk to vulnerable groups.
Relevant operators must cooperate as necessary with the market surveillance authority and relevant national public authorities or bodies when an evaluation of an AI system is being conducted.

Where a market surveillance authority finds an AI system does not comply with the Regulation, it must without undue delay require the relevant operator to take corrective actions to bring the AI system into compliance, withdraw it from the market, or recall it within a prescribed period not exceeding 15 working days.
exceptions: Shorter period may apply as provided for in relevant Union harmonisation legislation

obligations.summary: Where a market surveillance authority considers non-compliance is not restricted to its national territory, it must inform the Commission and other Member States without undue delay of the evaluation results and corrective actions required.
Operators must ensure that all appropriate corrective action is taken in respect of all AI systems concerned that have been made available on the Union market.

Where an operator fails to take adequate corrective action within the prescribed period, the market surveillance authority must take all appropriate provisional measures to prohibit, restrict, withdraw, or recall the AI system from the national market and notify the Commission and other Member States without undue delay.

Notifications of provisional restrictive measures must include all available details necessary to identify the non-compliant AI system, its origin and supply chain, the nature of the non-compliance and risk, and the nature and duration of the national measures taken, and must indicate the specific basis of non-compliance.

Market surveillance authorities other than the one initiating the procedure must without undue delay inform the Commission and other Member States of any measures adopted and additional information on non-compliance, and of any objections to notified national measures.

A provisional national measure is deemed justified if no objection is raised by a market surveillance authority or the Commission within three months of receipt of the notification, without prejudice to the operator's procedural rights; this period is reduced to 30 days for non-compliance with prohibited AI practices under Article 5.
exceptions: Period reduced to 30 days in cases of non-compliance with Article 5 prohibited AI practices
Without prejudice to procedural rights of the operator under Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020

obligations.summary: Market surveillance authorities must ensure that appropriate restrictive measures, such as withdrawal of the AI system from their market, are taken without undue delay in respect of non-compliant AI systems.
